newsitem.title: UK: U.K. approves development of Shell's Mallard field.
newsitem.headline: U.K. approves development of Shell's Mallard field.

text.p: The British government on Wednesday approved Shell U.K.'s plans to develop the Mallard oil and gas field in the central North Sea.

The field, which is expected to begin producing in October 1997, has estimated recoverable reserves of 25 million barrels of oil and 17 billion cubic feet of gas, the Department of Trade and Industry said.
Shell owns 38 percent of Mallard. The other equity holders are Esso (38 percent) and Total (24 percent).

Mallard, which will be developed using near horizontal drilling technology, will be tied back to Shell's Kittiwake platform from where oil will be offloaded by shuttle tanker and gas exported via the Fulmar platform to St Fergus.
The field, which is located 175 km northeast of Aberdeen in block 21/19 and was discovered in 1990, is expected to produce for eight years.
